info.title: Engram
info.description: The Engram control plane over HTTP (ADR 0027): every route calls the Plane. A server started with credentials (ADR 0042) takes a bearer API key or a JWT of its issuer and binds the request's actor to it; one started with --insecure-loopback answers on loopback with self-asserted actors.

Actor.description: Who acts: id, the level it reads as, its member scopes, and the provenance kind of what it writes. On a server with credentials (ADR 0042) the id and level must be the credential's and the memberships a subset of its own, and the source sent is ignored for the credential's; in process and under --insecure-loopback it is taken as the caller asserts it.

item.description: A MemoryItem (#/components/schemas/MemoryItem) as the caller assembles it; the plane validates it and denies an invalid one with the event engram/write/schema.

at.description: The time validity windows are judged at, UTC ISO 8601, when the reader asks what was true at another time. The read itself happens at the server's clock: its event's ts, and the time status, ttl and grant expiry are judged at. It sweeps nothing, and the read event's reason records it.

policy.description: The policy the read was decided under: <id> v<version>.

at.description: The time validity windows are judged at, UTC ISO 8601, when the reader asks what was true at another time. The read itself happens at the server's clock: its event's ts, and the time status, ttl and grant expiry are judged at. It sweeps nothing, and the read event's reason records it.

VisibleScope.description: A scope the actor can see: `membership`, a member scope the read matrix lets its level read; `grant`, otherwise, the scope of an item a read now admits through a live grant (card E8.14).

policy.description: The policy the listing was decided under: <id> v<version>.

StoreSync.description: What the workspace did before the read, as the store's owner: its retention sweep, then the adoption of the store's own memories (ADR 0025, decision D8).

counts.description: The counts the read event's reason records (core's readCounts, decision 5 of the Gate B plan); null for a read event written before that format. Audit data for the human inspector: out_of_reach counts items outside the reader's reach, which decision D5 keeps from the reader, so a surface that answers a model (the MCP tools, the pi extension) must not pass the counts on.

cut.description: Admitted items the read limit cut: present only on a read by a plane with the core retrieval pipeline and a limit.

ReadCounts.description: The counts a read event's reason records: returned of candidates, the filtered total and its categories, the admitted items a read limit cut (when the plane has one), and the projected items outside the reader's reach (never candidates).

add.description: Grants to add. Each must name a principal or a prefixed pattern, a class and an expiry after the call's time (ADR 0021, decision D4); the plane decides, and refuses one with a deny event.

remove.description: Grants to remove, each exactly as the item carries it.

scope.description: Every actor that is a member of this scope...

to.description: Every actor whose id the grant's `to` matches (exactly, or by prefix before a final `*`).

grant.description: The grant: to the item's owner by its place on the item, as a read's grants_used names it (`grants[<i>]:<to>`); to anyone else without its place (`grant:<to>`).

ReaderEntry.description: One entry of a who-can-read answer: every member of a scope reading as a level (the read matrix row that admits them), or every actor a live grant on the item names (the grant that admits them).

answered.description: False when the plane refuses to answer; every other field is then empty.

target.description: The item id or scope asked about, as given.

at.description: The time the answer is judged at: the read's access time, never before the log's head.

reason.description: Why the plane answered as it did, or why it refused.

readers.description: The symbolic reader set: an actor may read the target exactly when an entry admits it.

grants_shown.description: Which grants an item's answer shows: all to its owner, yours (only those naming the asker) to anyone else; null for a scope (grants are on items) and for a refusal.

closed.description: Why nobody may read the item now (its status, ttl or validity window), or null.

dormant.description: To the owner only: the item's grants that admit nobody now, each with why.

WhoCanReadAnswer.description: Who can read an item or a scope (card E2.13): a symbolic set of readers, each entry with the rule or grant that admits it, from the rules that decide a read. Answered only for an actor who may read the item or its scope; grant holders named to the item's owner only (decision item 53).

after.description: Only events with a seq above this one.

as.description: A key of the workload's actors.

item.description: The MemoryItem (#/components/schemas/MemoryItem) as the caller sent it; one that fails the schema replays as the plane's engram/write/schema denial.

as.description: A key of the workload's actors.
A key of the workload's actors.
A key of the workload's actors.
A key of the workload's actors.

Workload.description: A recorded workload (card E8.9): its actors by name and the plane calls it made, in order. Each write carries its whole item.

policy.description: The candidate policy; the workspace's own policy when absent. The baseline is always the workspace's.

SimReport.description: A workload replayed under the plane's policy (baseline) and a candidate policy, each on a scratch log and store: decisions, the utility proxy (items reads returned) and evictions per policy, and the steps that differ (card E8.9).

bearer.description: An Engram API key (egk_...) or a JWT access token of the server's issuer (ADR 0042)
